page: The Vultr voc-c-1c-2gb-25s-amd is a dedicated single-core instance belonging to the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 1 physical x86_64 core (1 vCPU, 1 thread) based on AMD EPYC architecture clocked at 2.0 GHz, backed by 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a generous 32 MB L3 cache pool. Vector processing is enabled through AVX, AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. Hardware resources include 2.0 GB of system memory (a 1:2 compute-to-RAM ratio), 25 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server includes no GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-threaded processing capabilities. The instance scored 3373.08 in stress-ng single-core tests, placing it in the top 10% bracket, and achieved strong throughput in single-threaded gzip compression (31.6 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.2 GB/sec). However, because capacity is bound to a single thread and 2.0 GB of RAM, aggregate throughput benchmarks register on the lower end. Multi-core stress-ng performance matches single-core results, while PassMark CPU (2955.8) and static web serving throughput (1.65 GB/sec) remain in the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth yields 35.29 GB/sec for uncached large reads and 32.48 GB/sec for writes.

The dedicated CPU allocation prevents noisy-neighbor resource competition typical of shared-core options, providing predictable execution times without CPU throttling. The compact memory footprint and single-thread limitation preclude high-concurrency database systems or memory-intensive services. This configuration represents an efficient resource profile for isolated utility tasks, lightweight CI/CD build runners, background queue workers, and small-scale automation scripts where dedicated CPU stability is required without provisioning unneeded multi-core overhead.
